commenti.body: Love these movies, I used to watch them with my friend all the time. They balance surrealism and goofiness perfectly and there's some genuinely interesting plot underneath all the silliness. I never saw the 5th film but I love how each film has a distinct vibe. The forth film in particular felt super eerie and dark, and made great use of cut footage from the original

As a horror and exploitation fan, I adore the Phantasm franchise. And have only grown to love them more as I get older. 

It's easily to dismiss them as standard 80s and 90s horror schlock, and they do purposefully lean into that, but they have this underlying sense of tragedy and despair to them that makes them unique among their peers. 

For some, the refusal to answer most of the questions and wrap things up definitively will be a huge issue. But I've come to view the series as a whole about the death of America, in a way. That may sound like a "iamverysmart" kinda take, but as the franchise progresses America becomes more and more desolate, hollowed out, unforgiving and dangerous. 

Granted, some of this is budgetary. But the atmosphere the films build up is quite potent. It's a story of the everyman  trapped in a vicious and never-ending cycle by the powers that be - the powers that seem to hold the fate of you, your brother, and your neighbors in the palm of his hand and uses his brainwashed work force drones to gain more power for powers sake.

 I don't think it's that far fetched a reading. 

And as fun, gory, humorous surrealist horror films - they excel. I love the dreamy nightmare logic vibes of the original. Just a really lowkey, atmospheric 70s freak-out of a film. Phantasm 2 and 3 are incredibly fun. Lord of the Dead especially deserves more love imo. So. Much. Fun. It feels like Coscarelli channeling a little bit of Raimi.

Oblivion returns to the more dreamy and slow burn aspect of the first, and not much happens- but it's got some of the most striking imagery in the series and it's really quite melancholy. 

I don't hate Ravager. Like all the films before it, they did what they could with what they had. And it shows a clear love for the characters. Would it have been nice if the final film had more $$$ behind it and ended things more concretely? Sure. But I think Ravager is an unpretentious love letter and goodbye to the series despite its obvious limitations.
